title: Posture Remediation Funnel — Detection-to-Compliant Conversion Rate
exclusions: Covers the detection logic documented for 'Posture Remediation Funnel — Detection-to-Compliant Conversion Rate' only. Does not replace full NAC policy design or firewall rule authoring or regulatory attestation. Entities listed in `network_exception_register.csv` during approved tests are excluded.
evidence: Saved search `network_posture_remediation_funnel_detection_to_complian` (UC-17.1.53), SOC dashboard panel "Network — Posture Remediation Funnel — Detection-to-Compliant Conversion Rate", and weekly export to `index=audit_evidence` sourcetype=csv:network_controls.

compliance.assurance_rationale: PCI 5.2 — anti-malware deployment. Posture validates anti-malware and remediates non-compliance.
PCI 6.3.3 — patch within 1 month. Posture's patch checks evidence ongoing patch cadence.
SI-3 (Malicious Code Protection) — posture validates protections.
A.8.7 (Protection against malware) — posture is one such control.
164.308(a)(5) Security Awareness and Training — including malware protection.

controlTest.positiveScenario: Ingest synthetic events into `index=nac` sourcetype='cisco:ise:syslog' where `endpoint_mac` satisfies detection threshold for UC-17.1.53 ('Posture Remediation Funnel — Detection-to-Compliant Conversion Rate'). Run the saved search and confirm at least one alertable row with expected fields populated.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Ingest benign `nac` / `cisco:ise:syslog` events where `endpoint_mac` stays below detection threshold, or exclude the test entity via `network_exception_register.csv` with a valid window. Confirm zero alert rows for UC-17.1.53.

dataSources: ISE syslog `index=nac sourcetype=cisco:ise:syslog` *Posture* category — codes `15041` (posture compliant), `15042` (posture non-compliant), `15043` (posture pending), `15044` (posture remediation initiated), `15045` (posture remediation completed), `15046` (posture remediation failed). Fields: `endpoint_mac`, `posture_policy`, `failed_condition`, `remediation_action`. CIM mapping: `Vulnerability.severity`.
spl:
index=nac sourcetype="cisco:ise:syslog" MessageCode IN (15042, 15044, 15045, 15046) earliest=-7d
| eval stage = case(MessageCode=="15042", "detected", MessageCode=="15044", "remediation_started", MessageCode=="15045", "remediation_completed", MessageCode=="15046", "remediation_failed")
| stats values(stage) as stages dc(_time) as event_count by endpoint_mac, posture_policy
| eval reached_compliance = if(mvfind(stages, "remediation_completed")>=0, "yes", "no")
| stats count as endpoints, sum(eval(if(reached_compliance=="yes",1,0))) as compliant by posture_policy
| eval conversion_pct = round((compliant/endpoints)*100, 1)
| sort conversion_pct
description: Tracks the posture-remediation funnel: how many endpoints flagged as non-compliant successfully reach a compliant state, broken down per posture policy. Exposes ineffective posture policies (low conversion rate) for tuning.
value: Tracks the posture-remediation funnel: how many endpoints flagged as non-compliant successfully reach a com.... Timely UC-17.1.53 alerting on 'Posture Remediation Funnel — Detection-to-Compliant Conversion Rate' reduces unauthorized access, segmentation drift, and NAC policy failures before manual triage or audit channels escalate.
implementation: Confirm *Posture* category at INFO. Schedule weekly summary report (Monday 06:00 UTC). For real-time per-endpoint tracking, schedule a 4h cadence search to populate a summary index `ise_posture_funnel` with per-endpoint state.
visualization: (1) Funnel chart: detected → remediation_started → remediation_completed. (2) Top-N: lowest-conversion-rate posture policies. (3) Trend: weekly conversion rate per policy.
knownFalsePositives:
1. **Certificate or EAP profile rollout** — Clients fail EAP-TLS during staged cert deployment for 'Posture Remediation Funnel — Detection-to-Compliant Conversion Rate'. Cross-check `FailureReason` and CMDB cert expiry.

2. **RADIUS/PSN maintenance restart** — Short auth failure burst while ISE node restarts. Match change window on `index=changes`.

3. **Guest or IoT onboarding surge** — Legitimate MAC registration spike skews `index=nac` `cisco:ise:syslog` baselines.

4. **Approved pen-test or scanner traffic** — Red-team exercises from netblock in `approved_scanners.csv` mimic auth failures.

**Suppression mechanism:** `network_exception_register.csv` keyed on `CallingStationID`, `NAS-IP-Address`, `valid_until`.
mitreAttack: N/A (posture remediation pipeline — measures policy compliance flow, no adversary technique)
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• ISE Posture configured.
• Posture agent deployed to endpoints.
• `posture_policies.csv` with `posture_policy`, `target_conversion_pct`.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Enable *Posture* category at INFO.

Step 2 — Create the search
Weekly search in `spl` field.

A secondary 4h cadence search populates summary index for trend analysis.

Step 3 — Validate
Provoke as above.

Step 4 — Operationalize
Dashboard "ISE — Posture Funnel":
• Funnel chart per policy.
• Top-N lowest conversion.
• Trend over 12 weeks.

Weekly review: posture team reviews lowest-conversion policies and tunes.

Step 5 — Troubleshooting
• **All policies show 0% conversion** — Posture agent not reaching endpoints; cross-ref UC-17.1.54.
• **One policy at 0%** — Remediation action mis-configured.
• **Trend declining** — New endpoint type incompatible with existing remediation.

Step 1 — Configure data collection

Install and configure the add-on referenced in the app field (`Splunk Add-on for Cisco Identity Services` ([Splunkbase 1915](https://splunkbase.splunk.com/app/1915)).). Enable the modular input or HEC token that writes sourcetype=cisco:ise:syslog into nac. Default poll interval 300–900 seconds unless the vendor API rate-limits lower. Grant the ingestion role `list_inputs` and `search` on the target index.

Step 2 — Create the search and alert

Schedule the SPL with earliest=-24h@h and throttle per entity to avoid duplicate pages. Document tunable macros in the comment header. Understanding this SPL: filters in the first pipeline reduce license cost; stats/timechart aggregates define the alert grain; joins/lookups enrich owner or asset metadata for routing.

Step 3 — Validate

Compare `| tstats count where index=... sourcetype=...` against the vendor admin UI inventory count (+/-5%). Spot-check two known entities for field presence (`endpoint_mac, posture_policy, reached_compliance, stage`). Run `timechart count span=1h` over 7 days to find ingestion gaps longer than two poll intervals.

Step 4 — Operationalize

Add a dashboard row with single-value KPI tiles, a 24-hour timechart, and a drilldown table mirroring the SPL output columns. Route critical severity to the platform on-call channel; route warning to the service owner from the lookup.

Step 5 — Troubleshooting

No events: verify forwarder connectivity, HEC token ACLs, and that the modular input appears in `index=_internal source=*splunkd*`. NULL fields: check props/transforms order and TA version. Fewer results than expected: confirm index allow-lists on the search head role and that `_time` uses the correct timezone. API errors: inspect splunkd.log for HTTP 401/429 from the vendor endpoint configured in inputs.conf.
grandmaExplanation: When ISE finds a sick computer (missing antivirus, missing patch), it tries to fix it before letting it on the network. We measure how many sick computers actually got fixed — the lower the number, the more useless the fix-up rules are.
